title: Zesty Malaysian Cutlet Curry
description: A bitter, crisp monsoon Malaysian dish featuring beef cutlets simmered in a zesty coconut tamarind sauce with crunchy nuka-pickle.
instructions: Pat the beef cutlets dry and season lightly with salt and pepper.
Coat each cutlet first in flour, then dip in beaten eggs, and finally roll in panko breadcrumbs until fully coated.
Heat 2 tablespoons of vegetable oil in a clay pot over medium-high heat and fry the cutlets until golden brown on both sides; remove and set aside.
In the same pot, add the remaining tablespoon of oil and sauté the spice paste for 30 seconds until fragrant.
Pour in the coconut milk and beef broth, stirring to combine and bring to a gentle simmer.
Add tamarind pulp, soy sauce, lime juice, and chili powder, whisking until the mixture thickens slightly.
Return the fried cutlets to the pot, spooning some sauce over them, and let them simmer for 5 minutes to absorb flavors.
Stir in the chopped nuka-pickle, reserving a small amount to garnish later.
Reduce heat to low, cover, and let the curry finish cooking for an additional 3 minutes.
Plate the cutlets with a drizzle of remaining sauce and a sprinkle of fresh cilantro if desired, serving hot.
